records.description:
White Bear Lake, MN
 
 
**About Heraeus**
Making displays foldable? Help hearts beat with micro-particles? Work on solutions involving precious metals? As a family-owned global technology group we help our customers to always being one step ahead.
 
 
**About Heraeus Medevio**
Heraeus Medevio combines medical technology expertise with collaborative partnerships. Together with medical device manufacturers, we develop and implement solutions for defined applications. As part of the Heraeus Group, we support the professional development of our employees and offer opportunities for career development, depending on the role, location and operational conditions.
 
 
To reach our vision of improving 100 million lives every year, we foster a culture of curiosity that thrives on challenge, continuous learning, growth, and the opportunity to try new things. With sites in the United States, European Union, and Asia, and over 2,200 employees worldwide, together, we will meet tomorrow's challenges today.
 
 
**Position Summary**
The Director, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering leads the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of advanced manufacturing technology across the Americas manufacturing network, including automation, digital manufacturing, and additive manufacturing. This role owns the design, development, validation, implementation, and maintenance of automated manufacturing equipment, assembly systems, robotics, vision inspection technologies, digital manufacturing solutions, and additive manufacturing processes and equipment that support the production of medical devices. The Director, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering role builds and leads a team of engineering professionals across these disciplines, sets technical direction and standards, and partners closely with Manufacturing, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, and Supply Chain to advance productivity, quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence across multiple sites.
 
 
**This is an onsite position at the White Bear Lake, MN location with travel to other global manufacturing sites.**
**What You’ll Do Every Day**

* Develop and execute the advanced manufacturing engineering roadmap (including automation, digital manufacturing, and additive manufacturing) aligned with business objectives.
* Establish long-term technology strategies to support manufacturing capacity expansion, cost reduction, and product quality improvement across the manufacturing network.
* Identify emerging technologies and evaluate opportunities for implementation, including robotics, AI-enabled inspection systems, Industry 4.0/digital manufacturing applications, advanced controls, and additive manufacturing processes and equipment.
* Lead capital equipment planning and investment strategy across automation, digital manufacturing, and additive manufacturing initiatives.
* Collaborate with Manufacturing, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, Supply Chain, and external technology partners to enhance productivity, quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.
* Direct a team responsible for automation engineering, controls engineering, robotics, machine vision, electrical engineering, digital manufacturing/manufacturing systems integration, and additive manufacturing.
* Build and mentor high-performing engineering teams through coaching, performance management, and talent development, while establishing engineering standards, best practices, and design methodologies across advanced manufacturing disciplines.
* Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws, including selection, training and development, assigning work, and performance management of employees.
* Manage complex, multidisciplinary engineering projects from concept through implementation, delivering on time and within budget while meeting technical and quality requirements, and communicate progress and issues clearly to leadership to support project and site objectives.
* Manage external automation, digital manufacturing, and additive manufacturing integrators, contractors, and equipment suppliers.
* Develop and control departmental operating and capital budgets; establish project schedules, resource plans, and cost controls.
* Other duties may be assigned as required.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Automation, or Industrial Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field required; Master’s degree in Engineering, MBA, or related discipline preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in automated manufacturing environments; experience in digital manufacturing and/or additive manufacturing strongly preferred.
* Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience managing engineering teams.
* Experience within medical device, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other highly regulated manufacturing industries.
* Proven success leading large-scale automation, digital manufacturing, and/or additive manufacturing projects and capital equipment installations.
* Experience with equipment validation and regulatory compliance in FDA-regulated environments.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams across multiple sites and drive continuous improvement and digitalization initiatives.
* Excellent communication, problem-solving, project management, and organizational skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel across the Americas manufacturing network (White Bear Lake, MN; Costa Rica; Puerto Rico), approximately 25-50% of the time.

*Medevio is committed to providing competitive total compensation and benefits packages. The expected hiring range for this position is between $160,000 and $190,000 based upon a full-time schedule. This is a good faith estimate on the applicable range. Base salaries are determined by taking a variety of factors in account, including, but not limited to, candidate qualifications, geographic locations, market conditions and internal equity. This position is bonus eligible, with a target bonus of 20%. Our total compensation package includes eligibility for comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company match, education reimbursement, paid parental leave and paid time off.*
**Curious? Apply now!**
Heraeus is proud to be an employer that provides equal access to opportunities for all its employees. We provide fair and equal consideration to all qualified applicants, regardless of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other legally protected characteristic. A diverse and inclusive culture is at the heart of our Vision, Mission, and Values. We are dedicated to cultivating a workforce that reflects a broad spectrum of cultures, backgrounds, and perspectives.
 
 
We participate in E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility after hire. Learn more at www.e-verify.gov
 
 
**Any further questions?**
If you need any assistance or have questions, please contact hrdirect-americas@heraeus.com or visit our website at jobs.heraeus.com.

records.title: Director of Engineering, Global Manufacturing Engineering & NPI
records.description:
The Director of Engineering leads Manufacturing Engineering, Process Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Test Engineering, Test Automation, NPI Engineering, and Customer TPM teams for a global data center rack manufacturing business. This role is responsible for engineering execution at the New Jersey manufacturing campus and for establishing global engineering standards, processes, and best practices across all manufacturing locations.
 
 
The Director drives manufacturing readiness, automation, operational excellence, quality, productivity, and successful new product introductions while partnering closely with customers and Platform Engineering. Platform Engineering retains ownership of product design, architecture, DFM approval, and Level 3 technical solutioning.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Manufacturing Engineering Leadership**

* Lead Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, Test Automation, NPI Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Customer TPM organizations.
* Establish and deploy global engineering standards, SOPs, governance, and best practices.
* Develop engineering talent, succession plans, and organizational capability.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Own engineering performance for the New Jersey campus and drive global engineering consistency.
* Optimize manufacturing flows, capacity, labor efficiency, throughput, and cycle time.
* Deliver improvements in FPY, RTPY, DPPM, OEE, cost, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive KPI management systems and operational review rigor.

**Automation & Test Strategy**

* Define and execute factory automation and smart manufacturing roadmaps.
* Lead deployment of robotics, vision systems, automated assembly, digital manufacturing, and Industry 4.0 solutions.
* Own manufacturing test strategy, test automation, diagnostics, traceability, and test system scalability.

**New Product Introduction (NPI)**

* Own manufacturing readiness throughout all NPI phase gates.
* Ensure readiness of processes, tooling, automation, test systems, capacity, and staffing.
* Lead pilot builds, manufacturing validation, launch readiness reviews, and production ramps.
* Identify and mitigate manufacturing risks to schedule, quality, and scalability.

**Customer & Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Lead customer-facing TPM teams and serve as executive engineering interface for strategic customers.
* Partner with Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Customers, and Platform Engineering to achieve successful product launches.
* Align manufacturing capabilities with customer requirements and growth plans.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA, and SPC methodologies.
* Lead cost reduction, productivity, yield improvement, and waste elimination initiatives.
* Build a culture of accountability, standardization, and continuous improvement.

**Ownership & Interfaces**
**This Role Owns**

* Manufacturing Engineering
* Process Engineering
* Industrial Engineering
* Test Engineering
* Test Automation
* Manufacturing readiness
* Factory readiness
* SOPs and engineering standards
* FPY, RTPY, DPPM, productivity, throughput, and operational KPIs
* Manufacturing validation and production ramp execution
* Customer TPM organization

**Partner Organizations**
**Platform Engineering**

* Product architecture and design
* Product specifications and BOM ownership
* DFM/DFA approval
* Product validation and qualification
* Design changes and reliability engineering
* Level 3 debugging, root cause analysis, and technical solution development

**Customers**

* Product requirements
* Acceptance criteria
* Product roadmap priorities
* Qualification and approval requirements

**Key Metrics**

* First Pass Yield (FPY)
* Rolled Throughput Yield (RTPY)
* DPPM
* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ)
* On-Time Delivery (OTD)
* Productivity and labor efficiency
* Manufacturing cycle time
* Automation ROI
* NPI launch success
* Customer satisfaction
* Global standards adoption

**Qualifications**

* BS in Engineering required; MS/MBA preferred.
* 15+ years of manufacturing engineering leadership experience.
* Experience leading Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, Automation, and NPI organizations.
* Proven success in high-volume electronics, server, rack integration, or data center manufacturing environments.
* Strong customer-facing leadership skills.
* Demonstrated track record improving FPY, RTPY, quality, productivity, and operational performance.
* Lean Six Sigma and global manufacturing experience preferred.

**Ideal Candidate**
A strategic and hands-on engineering leader capable of building a world-class global manufacturing engineering organization that delivers scalable NPI execution, advanced automation, operational excellence, and industry-leading quality for hyperscale and enterprise data center infrastructure products.
 
 
**About ZT Systems**
At ZT Systems, a Sanmina Company, you’ll get to do work you are proud of alongside smart, passionate people. Every day, there are opportunities to collaborate with the best in the industry to design, build, and deliver impactful solutions to world-class customers. Along the way, you will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment that’s challenging, rewarding, and career-defining.
 
 
A culture built around our values we work hard and think fast. We view challenges as opportunities—to do better, push harder, and be faster than we were the day before. When we fail, we learn from it and move on together. And when we succeed, we use the momentum to go even further. We create value with everything we do, building the foundation of today—and transforming the future of tomorrow.
 
 
Join ZT Systems and help us build technology infrastructure that connects the world.
 
 
**What We Offer**
At ZT Systems, a Sanmina Company, we believe that investing in our people is key to our continued growth and innovation. When you join our team, you’ll gain access to a comprehensive and inclusive benefits package designed to support your well-being, financial security, and professional development—both now and in the future.
 
 
**Compensation & Financial Security**

* Competitive base salary
* Performance-based annual bonus eligibility
* 401(k) retirement savings plan
* Tuition reimbursement for eligible education programs

**Health & Wellness**

* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with access to leading providers

-Mental health resources and employee wellness support programs-
 
 

* Company-paid life and disability insurance

**Time Away & Work-Life Balance**

* Paid time off (PTO) and company-paid holidays
* Parental leave and family care support programs

**Growth & Purpose**

* Structured training programs and on-the-job learning opportunities
* Matching gifts and volunteer programs to support causes you care about

These benefits are available to eligible employees and are designed to grow with you as your career evolves. Full benefits and eligibility varies by work location. Learn more about our benefits here.
 
 
ZT Group Int’l. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. ZT Systems provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
 
 
Please be aware that certain positions may require the applicant to either 1) be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C.
 
 

* 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C.
* 1158, or 2) be eligible to obtain an export control license or license exception from the Bureau of Industry and Science & U.S. Department of Commerce. All offers of employment will be conditional subject to the foregoing.

records.title: Senior Manager, Additive Manufacturing Operations
records.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.
 
 
Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.
 
 
Purpose
 
 
We are seeking an exceptional, results-driven
**Senior Manager of Additive Manufacturing Operations**
to lead and scale our Factory 1 production organization. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for driving world-class execution across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development while shaping the future of manufacturing.
 
 
The Additive Manufacturing organization leverages proprietary, state-of-the-art systems and processes to execute metal laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), depowdering, manual and automated support removal, surface finishing, heat treatment, and inspection across multiple factory sites supporting both prototype and high-rate production.
 
 
This role is ideal for an ambitious operations leader who thrives in fast-paced, high-growth environments and combines strong manufacturing fundamentals with data-driven decision making, automation, and continuous improvement. Beyond delivering daily operational performance, this leader will develop people, build scalable operating systems, and partner with engineering to industrialize new technologies that will define the next generation of manufacturing.
 
 
The ideal candidate is energized by difficult manufacturing challenges, inspires high-performing teams, and is passionate about building organizations capable of delivering exceptional results.
 
 
The Role
 
 
**Operational Leadership**

* Lead Factory 1 additive manufacturing operations to achieve world-class performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and equipment reliability.
* Build, develop, and mentor a high-performing team while fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement.
* Drive disciplined daily management through standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, and operational rigor.
* Optimize manufacturing flow by increasing equipment uptime, eliminating bottlenecks, improving process repeatability, and maximizing production throughput.
* Partner closely with Platform Development, Manufacturing Engineering, and Automation teams to successfully launch new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities.

**Operational Excellence**

* Champion Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement across all additive manufacturing processes.
* Establish scalable operating systems that improve efficiency, stability, and manufacturing readiness as production grows.
* Utilize manufacturing data, KPIs, and analytics to drive operational decisions and prioritize improvement initiatives.
* Develop meaningful performance dashboards and operating rhythms that enable rapid identification and resolution of production issues.
* Lead initiatives to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), first-pass yield, cycle time, labor productivity, and cost per part.

**Equipment Reliability & Technical Capability**

* Continue developing the in-house Additive Manufacturing Service organization by strengthening technical capability, preventive maintenance programs, troubleshooting processes, and technician training.
* Drive reliability initiatives that maximize printer availability, reduce unplanned downtime, and improve long-term equipment performance.
* Partner with technical teams to identify recurring equipment issues and implement sustainable corrective actions.

**Performance Monitoring & Compliance**

* Ensure strict adherence to Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), work instructions, process controls, and quality standards.
* Monitor key operational metrics and hold teams accountable for achieving business objectives.
* Drive disciplined root cause analysis and corrective actions to eliminate recurring manufacturing issues.
* Develop clear, actionable operational reporting that enables data-driven decision making across the organization.

**Safety, Quality & Financial Management**

* Foster a safety-first culture aligned with Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) standards and best practices.
* Partner with EHS to proactively develop and implement safety initiatives that reduce operational risk.
* Ensure manufacturing processes consistently meet internal quality requirements and applicable industry standards.
* Develop, manage, and execute the Factory 1 Additive Manufacturing operating budget while balancing productivity, cost, and long-term capability investments.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls.
* Demonstrated success leading complex manufacturing operations in high-performance production environments.
* Proven ability to build, develop, and lead high-performing technical organizations.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing, operational excellence, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Experience using manufacturing data and operational metrics to drive strategic decision making and measurable business results.
* Proven ability to execute in startup or rapidly scaling manufacturing environments while effectively navigating ambiguity and change.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance through equipment reliability, process optimization, and organizational development.
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Weld Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical experience).

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Leadership experience in metal additive manufacturing or other advanced manufacturing environments.
* Experience with Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) production systems.
* Experience with aerospace manufacturing standards, including AS9100 and NADCAP.
* Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Theory of Constraints, or similar operational excellence methodologies.
* Experience leading automation, Industry 4.0, MES, or digital manufacturing initiatives.
* Demonstrated success scaling manufacturing organizations through periods of rapid growth.

Pay Range: $156,640 USD - $215,380 USD
 
 
**What We Offer Our Regular, Full-Time Employees:**

* Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.
* Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.
* Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.
* Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.
* Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint.

***Equal Employment Opportunity***
*Divergent is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected characteristic. Divergent provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.*
*EEO Poster*
*In order to adjust to changes in our business, it may become necessary to add, remove or modify certain duties and responsibilities, or to reassign you to another job position. From time to time you may be asked to work on special projects or to assist with other work. Your cooperation and assistance in performing such additional work is expected.*
***E-Verify: Right to Work***
*Our company participates in E-Verify. E-Verify is a program that electronically confirms a candidate’s eligibility to work in the United States after completing the Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9). The information provided on the Form I-9 is compared to the records contained in the Social Security Administration and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) databases. This helps employers verify the identity and employment eligibility of newly hired employees.*
*Eligibility to Work Poster (English) | Eligibility to Work Poster (Spanish)*
***Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance (FCIHO)***
*Pursuant to the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance (FCIHO), we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.*
***No agencies, no solicitations, and no calls please.***

records.title: Senior Manager, Plant Operations
records.description:
At WK Kellogg Co, we exist to create joy and connection to inspire Gr-r-reat days. We believe that doing good is always good for business and we have stood for this since Kellogg Company was founded more than 120 years ago. We are passionate about doing our part to make nutritious foods, create social connectivity and respect natural resources. Together, these actions create positive progress for people and the planet – today and for years to come. We have big plans for how we are going to accomplish this, and we would love for you to join us in this effort.
 
 
**The most compelling leadership opportunities aren’t always about stepping into something already built. Sometimes they’re about helping shape what comes next.**
The
**Senior Manager, Plant Operations**
leads the strategic and operational direction of multiple business units within a high-performing, large-scale, 24/7 manufacturing operation, and line-centric manufacturing platform.
 
 
This role drives excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development by empowering Operations Managers, Supervisors, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
 
 
**You won’t simply inherit an operation. You’ll have the opportunity to help build what comes next.**
**Working Relationships Include**

* Reports to: Plant Director
* Supervises: Operations Managers and Supervisors
* Peer Relationships: KSUM, Quality Manager, Sr. RM Manager, HR Manager, EHS Manager, E& F Manager, KIWS Coach
* Key Contacts: Internal – Plant Leadership Team, Corporate Operations, Engineering, KIWS, HR; External – Vendors, Contractors, and Corporate Support Functions

**Here’s What You Will Be Doing**

* Strategic Leadership: Set direction and priorities for assigned business units, ensuring alignment with plant goals and corporate strategy.
* Team Development: Lead, coach, and develop Operations Managers and Supervisor to build high-performing teams and future leaders.
* Operational Oversight: Ensure consistent execution of production plans and consistently deliver strong results across key plant KPIs, including safety, quality, food safety, cost, and service.
* Innovation & Project Execution: Lead the excellent execution of innovation and projects entering the plant, ensuring effective planning, cross-functional alignment, and successful implementation.
* Budgeting & Planning: Own the business planning and budgeting process for assigned units, including cost containment and resource allocation.
* Lean & CI Deployment: Champion and sustain lean manufacturing principles and WK Kellogg Integrated Work Systems (KIWS) across all units.
* Culture & Engagement: Drive a culture of safety, accountability, and engagement, promoting continuous learning and recognition.
* Compliance & Standards: Ensure compliance with all regulatory and internal standards related to safety, food safety, sanitation, and labor relations.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with support functions and external stakeholders to optimize performance and resolve complex challenges.

**Work Environment**

* This role is based within a 24/7 union manufacturing facility.
* Must be flexible to work any shift and travel up to 25%
* Regular presence on the production floor required
* Frequent interaction with internal teams and external partners

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing
* Proven success in leading large teams and managing multiple production lines
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement systems
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others and build effective teams
* Excellent strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
* Experience in union environments preferred
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and SAP
* Experience with budget creation and performance management
* Experience working within a 24/7 manufacturing environment is preferred

***Salary Range:***

*$164,160 - $205,200*
*Salary pay ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, certifications, qualifications, relevant education or training, and local market conditions.*
*At WK Kellogg Co, our success depends on our most vital asset — our people. That’s why we’re committed to providing you with benefits and programs that support your Total Health and your journey to be and feel your best — physically, financially, emotionally, and socially.*
*Although subject to change, the below are the benefits currently offered in association with this position:*

* Incentive Plan bonus eligibility
* Health, dental and vision insurance
* Savings and Investment Plan with Company match and contribution
* Paid Time Off (includes paid sick time)
* 11 Paid Holidays
* Life Insurance, AD and D Insurance and STD/LTD
* Tuition reimbursement, adoption assistance for eligible employees
* Employee recognition program

*The above offerings are subject to the terms of WKKC policies, which will control in the event of a conflict with the above descriptions*
*Our comprehensive and competitive benefits not only deliver value to you and your family, but also offer choice to meet your unique needs and knowledge to empower confident decision-making.*
**About Wk Kellogg Co**
*At WK Kellogg Co, we bring our best to everyone, every day through our trusted foods and brands. Our journey began in 1894, when our founder W.K. Kellogg reimagined the future of food with the creation of Corn Flakes, changing breakfast forever. Since then, we have embraced the same spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship in everything we do, channeling our founder’s passion and commitment to creating high quality and delicious products while fostering communities. Our iconic brand portfolio includes Frosted Flakes, Rice Krispies, Froot Loops, Kashi, Special K, Raisin Bran, Frosted Mini Wheats, and Bear Naked. With a presence in the majority of households across North America, our brands play a key role in enhancing the lives of millions of consumers every day, promoting a strong sense of physical, emotional and societal wellbeing. Our beloved brand characters, including Tony the Tiger and Toucan Sam, represent our deep connections with the consumers and communities we serve. For more information, visit*
*www.wkkellogg.com*
*.*

*If we can help you with a reasonable accommodation throughout the application or hiring process, please email TalentAssist@wkkellogg.com*
***THE FINER PRINT***
*The ability to work a full shift, come to work on time, work overtime as needed and the ability to work according to the necessary schedule to meet job requirements with or without reasonable accommodation is an essential function of this position.*
*WK Kellogg Co is an Equal Opportunity Employer that strives to provide an inclusive work environment, a seat for everyone at the table, and embraces the diverse talent of its people. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, disability, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, sexual orientation, age, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.*
**For US Applicants**
*Where required by state law and/or city ordinance; this employer will provide the Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), with information from each new employee’s Form I-9 to confirm work authorization. For additional information, please follow this*

*link*
*.*

records.title: Senior Manager of Operations
records.description:
**Senior Manager of Operations - Austin, TX**

**DESCRIPTION:**

We’re seeking a hands-on Sr. Operations Manager with experience scaling silicon-based products in a semiconductor company. This player-coach role owns the operational path from foundry and wafer production through test, backend processing, and manufacturing. You’ll qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, establish and strengthen quality-control measures, and drive consistent quality, yield, cost, and delivery as production grows.

Experience with RFID inlay production is especially relevant.

**What you’ll do:**

* Own foundry relationships from negotiation through production execution, and scale wafer level production.
* Manage wafer-test facility relationships; evaluate and qualify test partners, and select test equipment to optimize cost, quality, and throughput.
* Lead test development, wafer backend operations, yield improvement, reliability, and failure analysis.
* Qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, including overseeing end-to-end inlay production and its ramp to volume.
* Establish and improve quality-control measures, operating procedures, and RMA processes.
* Monitor supplier quality, conduct supply-chain audits, and resolve manufacturing, quality, and delivery issues.
* Establish and improve ERP/MRP processes, WIP tracking, inventory planning, and production controls.
* Develop cost models, negotiate contracts, and drive improvements in cost, quality, and delivery.
* Manage one direct report and coordinate work across four internal engineers and executive stakeholders, including the CEO.

**What you’ll bring:**

* BSEE or equivalent practical experience.
* 7–10 years of operations, manufacturing, or related experience in a semiconductor company.
* Experience with RFID inlay manufacturing is a plus.
* Hands-on experience with silicon-based products and semiconductor manufacturing operations.
* Experience scaling products from wafer fabrication and test through backend processing and volume production.
* Experience working with foundries, wafer-test facilities, and manufacturing vendors.
* Familiarity with yield optimization, reliability, quality assurance, supplier audits, failure analysis, ERP/MRP systems, WIP tracking, and inventory planning.
* Strong communication, coordination, and negotiation skills, with a practical, roll-up-your sleeves approach.

records.title: Senior Manager, Quality Engineering - Manufacturing Operations (2nd Shift)
records.description:
The
**Senior Manager, Quality Engineering (2nd Shift)**
is a people leadership and manufacturing quality role responsible for providing quality and compliance oversight across second-shift operations. This leader will manage and develop a team of Quality Engineers while partnering closely with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturing activities are performed safely, effectively, and in compliance with applicable quality system requirements.
 
 
The position will oversee quality and compliance activities supporting the plant’s major production areas, including THV manufacturing, TMTT manufacturing, advanced catheters, and metals. The successful candidate will strengthen NCR and CAPA execution, improve investigation quality, monitor operational quality metrics, and establish effective communication and continuity between first- and second-shift teams.
 
 
***This position supports our 2nd-shift operation (Monday - Thursday, 3:30 PM - 2:30 AM).***
**How You'll Make an Impact:**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of Quality Engineers supporting second-shift manufacturing operations, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Provide quality and compliance oversight for second-shift manufacturing activities, ensuring operations are performed in accordance with approved procedures, quality system requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Oversee the initiation, investigation, review, approval, and timely closure of nonconformance reports, including evaluating investigation quality, root cause determination, corrective actions, and product or process risk.
* Own and provide leadership for CAPAs, including investigation strategy, root cause analysis, action planning, implementation, effectiveness verification, and sustainable closure.
* Lead the deployment, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality management systems and manufacturing quality processes aligned with ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820.
* Review and approve test method validations, measurement system analyses, and manufacturing process validations, including IQ, OQ, and PQ documentation.
* Monitor quality metrics, trends, investigation performance, and quality data reviews; identify emerging risks and provide actionable recommendations to Operations and Quality leadership.
* Support internal and external audits by ensuring second-shift operations remain inspection-ready, responding to auditor questions, and leading or supporting actions resulting from audit observations.
* Partner with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to resolve quality issues, maintain compliant production, and strengthen operational controls.
* Establish effective shift-to-shift communication and escalation processes to ensure timely transfer of quality, production, and compliance information.
* Provide quality leadership for supplier-related issues, as applicable, including investigation support, corrective actions, and supplier performance concerns.
* Promote a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management throughout second-shift operations.
* Develop and implement quality processes that improve product compliance, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Other incidental duties as assigned.

**What You'll Need (Required):**

* Bachelor’s degree with relevant Quality Engineering, Quality Management, or Manufacturing Quality experience within a highly regulated environment; or equivalent experience based on Edwards’ criteria.
* Demonstrated people leadership experience managing and developing engineers or other technical quality professionals.
* Experience deploying, implementing, or sustaining quality management systems within a regulated manufacturing environment, including working knowledge of ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820 requirements.
* Strong experience leading CAPAs, nonconformance investigations, and structured root cause analysis, including evaluation of investigation quality and effectiveness.
* Ability to work onsite during the designated second-shift schedule, Monday through Thursday, 3:30 PM to 2:30 AM.

**What Else We Look For (Preferred):**

* Engineering or Scientific degree
* Medical device manufacturing experience
* Experience providing quality oversight for manufacturing or production operations, including partnering directly with Operations and Engineering to resolve compliance and product quality issues.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret quality data, monitor operational quality metrics, recognize adverse trends, and escalate significant risks.
* Experience with microbiology principles or microbiological controls in a regulated manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting cleanroom qualification, environmental controls, or manufacturing operations performed within controlled environments.
* Supplier quality or supplier management experience, including supplier investigations and corrective actions.
* Experience reviewing or approving test method validations and measurement system analysis studies.
* Experience reviewing or approving manufacturing process validations, including IQ/OQ/PQ.
* Experience supporting internal, external, or regulatory audits.
* Experience leading quality activities across multiple manufacturing technologies, product lines, or production areas.
* Knowledge of statistical methods, process capability, measurement systems, risk management, and continuous improvement tools.
* Demonstrated success strengthening team capability, improving organizational effectiveness, and leading change within a manufacturing quality organization.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence decisions and communicate effectively across technical, operational, and leadership audiences.

Edwards is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer including protected Veterans and individuals with disabilities.

records.title: Senior Manager, Quality
records.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Office
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
**LOCATION**
: On-site Logan, UT.
 
 

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**POSITION SUMMARY:**
The Senior Manager, Quality for BEA and Flexible Operations at the Logan, Utah site is responsible for leading site quality operations and ensuring compliance, product quality, and continuous improvement across manufacturing processes supporting flexible single-use technologies and products. This role partners closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and site leadership to drive operational excellence, maintain regulatory compliance, and support business growth.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Quality will lead quality teams responsible for manufacturing quality, quality systems, and customer quality activities while fostering a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and customer focus.
 
 
**WHAT YOU WILL DO:**
**Site Quality Leadership:**

* Lead and develop the site quality organization supporting BEA and Flexible Operations manufacturing activities.
* Establish and maintain a strong quality culture focused on compliance, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a key member of the Logan site leadership team, contributing to strategic and operational decision-making.
* Drive accountability through quality metrics, performance management, and development planning.
* Mentor and coach quality leaders and team members to build organizational capability.

**Quality Systems:**

* Ensure site compliance with applicable global regulatory requirements, industry standards, and internal quality management systems.
* Maintain site inspection readiness, including support for customer, notified body, and regulatory agency audits.
* Oversee effectiveness of Flexible site quality systems including: CAPA, Change control, Nonconformance management, Complaint handling, Document control, Training compliance, Risk management and Validation activities
* Drive timely and effective investigations, root cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Support implementation and harmonization of divisional quality initiatives and procedures.

**Operational Quality Support:**

* Partner cross functionally to reduce cost of poor quality and improve operational efficiency.
* Utilize data analytics and quality metrics to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities.
* Support product transfers, capacity expansions, and new product introductions
* Ensure robust investigation practices and timely resolution of deviations and customer concerns.
* Build strong customer relationships through responsiveness, transparency, and quality performance.

**HOW YOU WILL GET HERE:**
**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Chemistry, Quality, or related technical discipline required
* Advanced degree preferred
* 8+ years of progressive quality experience within regulated manufacturing environments
* 3+ years of leadership experience managing quality teams
* Experience in medical device, bioprocessing, pharmaceutical, life sciences, or single-use manufacturing environments preferred
* Strong knowledge of quality systems and regulatory requirements including ISO 9001, ISO 13485, GMP, and FDA regulations

**Technical & Leadership Competencies:**

* Strong leadership and team development capabilities
* Proven ability to drive quality improvements in manufacturing environments
* Expertise in root cause analysis, CAPA, risk management, and quality systems
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
* Ability to influence and build strong partnerships across functions
* Experience supporting audits and regulatory inspections
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

**Key Success Metrics:**

* Audit outcomes
* Reduction in nonconformance and quality events
* CAPA effectiveness and closure timeliness
* Customer complaint reduction and responsiveness
* Employee engagement and talent development
* Continuous improvement and cost reduction results

**Leadership Expectations:**

* Demonstrate integrity, accountability and customer focus
* Lead through collaboration, communication and empowerment
* Foster a culture of quality, safety and continuous improvement
* Operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed, global organization
* Displays the Thermo Fisher 4i values of Innovation, Integrity, Intensity and Involvement

**Travel Requirements:**

* Travel up to 10% as required for business support, training and collaboration across sites

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.
 
 
Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

records.description:
**Description**
Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Department: EHSQ / Quality
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality
 
 
Direct Reports: None
 
 
FLSA Status: Exempt
 
 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
 
 
Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote
 
 
Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
 
 
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
 
 
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on high-voltage, substation, and transmission construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on HV and substation scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers collector substations, switchyards and points of interconnection, and generation tie-lines (gen-tie); medium-voltage collection systems remain within the scope of Electrical Quality.
 
 
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active HV, substation, or gen-tie construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of HV and substation Quality across the portfolio.
 
 
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors, combined with the judgment to translate engineering, utility, manufacturer, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and Transmission & Distribution (T&D) teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, relay and protection settings, and functional commissioning remain with Engineering and Commissioning; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
 
 
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time."
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on HV, substation, switchyard, point of interconnection, and gen-tie construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for HV and substation scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, utility requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain HV and substation inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.
* Integrate with the assigned Regional Quality Manager on each project containing HV, substation, or gen-tie scope, from pre-mobilization planning through turnover, confirming discipline requirements are incorporated into the Site-Specific Quality Management Plan (SSQMP), ITPs, inspection staffing plan, and inspection schedule.
* Support the Preconstruction Quality SME by tailoring discipline ITPs and checklists for project kickoff packages and identifying HV and substation-specific contract, utility, testing, and special inspection requirements.
* Provide technical direction to the HV & Substation Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors assigned to projects, in coordination with the Site Quality Manager, who retains administrative supervision and day-to-day site direction.
* Participate in recruitment, technical interviewing, onboarding, and qualification of discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, and provide performance input to the Site Quality Manager and Regional Quality Manager.
* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, documentation requirements, and common HV and substation failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the HV and substation Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for HV, substation, and gen-tie scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring HV and substation nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.
* Exercise stop-work authority for quality-driven conditions in accordance with company policy, coordinating through the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact on site.
* Elevate unresolved technical disagreements with site Quality, Construction, or subcontractor personnel to the Regional Quality Manager and Senior Director of Quality, with a documented position and recommended resolution.
* Define Quality’s verification requirements for receiving, storage, preservation, handling, and installation of major HV equipment, including power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, and control enclosures, in alignment with manufacturer requirements.
* Review acceptance test records and third-party test reports for completeness and conformance with ANSI/NETA ATS, project specifications, and manufacturer requirements, and coordinate Quality witness points with testing agencies and Commissioning.
* Define and support Quality’s responsibilities within the functional testing and cold commissioning RACI and in energization-readiness and turnover verification for HV and substation systems, while maintaining clear separation from relay settings, protection coordination, and functional commissioning responsibilities.
* Where required by contract and as directed by the Senior Director of Quality, support factory acceptance test (FAT) witnessing and source inspection of major HV equipment, and contribute to the development of a formal source inspection program as the organization establishes one.
* Coordinate with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, and third-party agencies on HV and substation Quality matters, including utility inspection and witness requirements for facilities built to utility standards.
* Align closely with the Engineering and T&D teams to resolve technical questions, participate in design and constructability reviews, and maintain consistent acceptance criteria across projects.
* Monitor HV and substation Quality KPIs and nonconformance trends across the portfolio, and report findings, emerging risks, and recommendations to the Senior Director of Quality.
* Provide input on discipline staffing and resource planning, including the number and qualification of Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors and third-party testing needs, for estimating and project staffing plans.
* Define the HV and substation Quality records required for turnover and verify completeness of discipline turnover documentation.
* Capture lessons learned from executed projects and incorporate them into discipline templates, training, and the broader Quality Management System (QMS).
* Interact and collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, T&D, Construction, Commissioning, Subcontract Management, and Safety teams to embed Quality into project execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned.
* Travel is required up to 50%, including scheduled jobsite visits, extended site visits, short-notice trips, and overnight stays.

**Key Competencies / Core Skills**

* Recognized technical authority who guides others through credibility and clear reasoning rather than positional authority.
* Translates engineering, manufacturer, utility, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria.
* Builds standardized tools, including ITPs, checklists, SWIs, and Procore templates, that scale across projects, regions, and delivery models.
* Leads effectively within a matrixed structure, supporting the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact while holding the technical standard for the discipline.
* Holds the standard under schedule and commercial pressure while maintaining professional, collaborative working relationships.
* Understands the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, electrical testing, protection and control, and Commissioning, and escalates appropriately.
* Maintains exceptional attention to detail across inspection records, test reports, and supporting objective evidence.
* Analyzes deficiency trends across the portfolio and translates findings into durable process change.
* Communicates clearly and factually with field personnel, engineers, utilities, owners, and executive leadership, both in writing and in person.
* Coaches and develops discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, treating development of the bench as a core responsibility.
* Manages multiple concurrent projects, travel demands, and shifting priorities while maintaining accountability.
* Maintains composure and a solutions-focused approach under pressure, disagreement, and challenging field conditions.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive quality experience in utility-scale renewable-energy, utility, substation, transmission, or industrial electrical construction, including at least 5 years of direct Quality responsibility on high-voltage substation or transmission projects; utility-scale PV electrical experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
* At least 5 years in a quality leadership or management role, including directing inspection personnel or leading Quality programs across multiple projects.
* Demonstrated experience authoring and maintaining ITPs, Quality Inspection Checklists, Standard Work Instructions, and procedures for HV and substation construction.
* Strong working knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, station service equipment, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors.
* Demonstrated ability to read and apply IFC drawings, one-line and three-line diagrams, grounding plans, physical arrangement drawings, schematics and wiring diagrams, cable schedules, specifications, approved submittals, and manufacturer instructions.
* Experience reviewing electrical acceptance test documentation and third-party test reports against ANSI/NETA ATS and project specifications.
* Experience overseeing Quality on both self-performed and subcontracted HV and substation work, including review of subcontractor Quality Control Plans and ITPs.
* Experience coordinating Quality activities with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, testing agencies, and equipment manufacturers.
* Demonstrated experience with nonconformance management, root cause analysis methodology (5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, or equivalent), and corrective action programs.
* Demonstrated understanding of the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, protection and control, and Commissioning responsibilities.
* Proficiency with Procore (Quality & Field Management modules) and SharePoint.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
* Ability to work remotely with a reliable high-speed internet connection and flexibility to support projects across Eastern through Pacific Time Zones as required.
* Must hold and maintain a valid U.S. driver’s license and have the ability to safely operate a motor vehicle, including the ability to rent vehicles for business travel without restrictions that would interfere with job performance.
* Ability to successfully pass a motor vehicle/driving record background check in accordance with company policy.
* Must be able to pass pre-employment, regular, and random drug and alcohol screenings in compliance with company and customer requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional certifications such as:

+ American Society for Quality (ASQ): Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Construction Quality Manager (CCQM), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA)
+ InterNational Electrical Testing Association (NETA): NETA Certified Technician, Level III or Level IV
+ American Welding Society (AWS): Certified Welding Inspector (CWI)
+ American Concrete Institute (ACI): Concrete Field Testing Technician, Grade I
+ Electrical licensing: State journeyman or master electrician license
+ Project Management Institute (PMI): Project Management Professional (PMP)

* Experience witnessing factory acceptance testing or performing source inspection of power transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, or control enclosures.
* Experience across multiple substation configurations, voltage classes, and equipment manufacturers, including facilities built to interconnecting utility standards and transferred to utility ownership.
* Experience with gen-tie transmission line construction, including foundations, steel structures, conductor and OPGW installation, and associated hardware.
* Working knowledge of NESC (IEEE C2), NEC (NFPA 70), ANSI/NETA ATS, IEEE 80, and IEEE C57 series standards for power transformers.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects with integrated substation and interconnection scopes.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
 
 

* Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while operating a computer and reviewing documentation, drawings, and test records.
* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, utilities, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to conduct regular jobsite visits requiring extended standing and walking on uneven or unpaved terrain, as well as bending, stooping, kneeling, and climbing stairs or ladders to access substation and HV construction areas.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds of inspection equipment, documentation, or other work-related materials as required.
* Ability to perform field activities while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and arc-rated clothing or other project-specific PPE where required.
* Ability to safely access substation and HV construction areas in accordance with site safety requirements, electrical safe-work practices, qualification requirements, and access controls.
* Ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time, including by air, with flexibility for short-notice trips, overnight stays, and extended site visits.
* Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
 
 

* Work is divided between a remote/home office environment, requiring reliable high-speed internet and standard office equipment, including audio/video conferencing, and active construction sites.
* Field work is performed at utility-scale substation, high-voltage, gen-tie, solar, and BESS construction sites, where conditions may include outdoor weather exposure, dust, moderate to high noise levels, moving construction equipment, and uneven terrain. Appropriate PPE will be provided and required.
* Field work regularly occurs in proximity to energized or potentially energized facilities as projects progress toward energization, requiring strict adherence to electrical safety requirements, qualification boundaries, and access controls.
* Work schedules during jobsite visits may vary based on construction activities, testing schedules, utility requirements, and project milestones, and may include early starts, extended hours, or weekends.
* Regular interaction with cross-functional teams in both virtual and in-person settings, requiring adaptability to both independent and collaborative work environments.

records.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.
 
 
For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.
 
 
At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.
 
 
We are looking for a S
**r. Manager, Quality**
to join our team in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This role will report to
**Director of Quality**
and based in
**Newark, Delaware. This is a fully on-site, in office role 5 days a week**
.
 
 
**Role and Responsibilities:**

* Ensure 100% Quality assurance at the Skid line manufacturing through inspection, testing, and sub-component testing/inspection. Assist in hiring personnel needed to support this effort.
* Partner with Install Quality team (field) to understand real time (daily) what items are escaping the plant and instituting immediate mitigation plans including addressing any inventory in the pipeline not yet installed.
* Implement permanent corrective actions working with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply chain, or SQE as per relevance on each issue.
* Provide quality input into the new equipment being purchased for the scaling of Delaware manufacturing. Include inputs for quality assurance into equipment design, and verification of process steps. Understand and provide input into the planned operation, what can be bypassed, maintenance plans, calibration or drift of the equipment, automation that can fail and be undetected leading to quality escapes.
* Participate and understand results from testing in the plant; Functional test, Tommy test, FIT, etc. Drive pareto of failures to help cross functional problem solving of test failures.
* Implement a 100% functional test (new) on skid final product assembly; electrical continuity, communications integrity, piping assurance, start up simulation, etc. to assure 100% QA prior to shipping to customer.
* Ensure skid components and systems have latest FW revision prior to shipping to the W/H, or out of W/H to field.
* Work with CIG and Manufacturing Engr, and NPI to implement workload being removed from the customer install side and being moved into skid assembly. Provide oversight to ensure best quality achievement; ensure work instructions are clear, operators trained, workstations have proper tools, and judgement criteria.
* Collaborate with Supplier Quality / Suppliers to achieve zero-defect flow (“dock-to-stock”) for all purchased, contract manufacture parts, materials, and Bloom Energy manufactured parts.
* Drive component and design failures back to the earliest point of detection in the process.
* Ensure manufacturing process have Control plans with CTQ, and POA built in to each station.
* Work collaboratively with Design teams to DFM, through a “registration system”, and Pokeyoke assembly methods for highest quality assurance.
* Drive test excellence in the manufacturing plan to ensure that equipment and test stations are certified with robust qualification programs, that are documented and controlled for changes with proper accuracy and gage R&R techniques.
* Drive yield task forces to achieve company wide targets at each manufacturing point under this scope, with cross functional teams driving top pareto issues to RCCA.
* Ensure early engagement with the product engineering team to teach and perform early stage risk assessments (DFMEA et.al.)
* Design for manufacturability and reliability improvements during the early design stages of product development.
* Work with Engineering NPI and the manufacturing engineering teams to perform PFMEA, write work instructions, and establish quality check-points to guarantee zero-defect quality in production.
* Develop and implement formal, comprehensive process documentation including process flow diagrams, Process FMEAs, process control plans, operations method Sheets, manufacturing quality charts (MQCs) and etc.
* Lead critical problem solving task forces with emphasis on cross functional inputs, accountability, time to RCCA, and ensurance of mitigation of inventory, or field units at risk.
* Troubleshoot product issues by reviewing engineering drawings and design requirements. Drive a rigorous resolution process for product quality, reliability and design issues.
* Perform data-driven root cause failure analyses for design, manufacturing, and administrative problems.
* Perform process audits to monitor, continuously improve, and sustain superior product quality.
* Demonstrate the ability to interface and work collaboratively across departments internally and with suppliers and customers, (including Purchasing, Quality, R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Marketing and Finance), while building strong and cooperative working relationships.
* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Establish and govern site COPQ metrics (scrap, rework, sorting, and warranty risk); lead cross-functional yield-improvement blitzes targeting measurable cost reductions and scrap minimization.
* Process Capability & Zero-Defect Mentality: Drive process capability (C\_p / C\_{pk} \ge 1.33) across critical-to-quality (CTQ) operations (welding, brazing, ceramic stack assembly, plumbing/gas-delivery, and electrical integration).

**Skills and Experience:**

* More than 10 years of increasing responsibility in the areas of Quality, and Manufacturing .
* Experience implementing company-wide ISO 9001 procedures and TS16949 standards and related process documentation. Possess working knowledge of process capability and control requirements, methods and systems.
* Demonstrated track record of building, restructuring, or significantly scaling a manufacturing quality team during rapid production ramp-up
* Proven successful application of multi-discipline engineering problem solving techniques.
* Understand the critical elements of modern Manufacturing Statistical Process Control, (e.g., practical working knowledge and experience with SPC, Process Capability, Cp, Cpk, etc.)
* Understand the critical elements of modern Reliability Engineering, (e.g., MCF, MTBF, MTT, etc.)
* Certification in a recognized problem-solving methodology such as six-sigma Black Belt, 8D, or Global Problem Solving.
* Strong verbal/active listening/written communications.
* Demonstrate planning and leadership skills.
* Expert with metrology, calibration, and Gage R & R’s.
* Ability to train in Quality System Auditing.
* Fluent in product phase-gate, NPI and technology transfer.
* Expertise in applying PPAP, First Article Inspections (FAI) and Reports).
* Strong critical thinking, analytical skills, and problem solving.
* Ability to effectively work within a very intense, dynamic, fast-paced, and demanding work environment.
* Familiarity with industry codes and quality standards applicable to clean power systems (ISO 9001:2015 required; working knowledge of ASME, NFPA, or UL standards preferred).
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality / Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) and ASQ Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) alongside CQE and Six Sigma Black Belt.
* Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite and statistical software.
* Possess a passion for excellence.
* Unrestricted willingness to travel to all regions. Travel may be up to 25% of time.
* BS, MS or PhD in Mechanical/Material Science/Chemical/Electrical/Systems Engineering.
* Direct experience managing high-temperature fluidics/gas delivery, welding/brazing, ceramic integration, power electronics, or structural enclosures is a strong plus.

Bloom Energy is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We are committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants, will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability. Bloom Energy makes reasonable accommodations, consistent with applicable laws, for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant or employee with a disability, who can perform the essential job functions, unless undue hardship would result.
 
 
At Bloom Energy, we are committed to supporting the well-being of our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees includes competitive Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with a large employer contribution, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, generous Mental Health Support services, Legal services, virtual Physical Therapy access, and Fertility & Family Forming benefits.
 
 
Bloom Energy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The total compensation for this position includes standard company benefits and is based on various factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience.
 
 
Salary Ranges:
 
 
$149,300.00 - $214,700.00
